American Express operates globally, with its 10-K geographic disclosures organized around the United States (its largest market) and international regions: Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA); Asia Pacific, Australia and New Zealand (APAC/JAPA); and Latin America, Canada and the Caribbean (LACC).

Operating margin is not a meaningful metric for American Express: as a bank holding company/payments lender it reports revenues net of interest expense and has no "operating income" line, with provisions for credit losses and funding costs driving profitability. Using the closest analogue, pretax margin (pretax income / revenues net of interest expense), 2022 was roughly 19% (about $9.9B pretax on $52.9B revenues) versus roughly 23% in 2021 (about $9.8B on $42.4B), so margins compressed as credit provisions normalized even though revenues grew strongly (~25%). Better metrics for AMEX are ROE (~32% in 2022), net interest margin, provision/reserve rates, and the efficiency ratio.

Gross margin is not a meaningful metric for American Express. As a financial services/payments company and bank holding company, Amex does not sell physical goods and reports no cost of goods sold or gross profit in its 10-K; instead it reports total revenues net of interest expense (discount revenue, net card fees, net interest income, travel commissions) against provisions for credit losses and operating expenses such as card member rewards and services. Profitability is better assessed via net interest margin, expense-to-revenue ratios, pretax margin, ROE and credit metrics.
